item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q024_fibronectin_fragment_selection","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, both domains are assigned to family b.1.2.1 (Fibronectin type III), within superfamily b.1.2, fold b.1 (immunoglobulin-like beta-sandwich), and class b (all-beta proteins). d1uc6a1 is the C-terminal cytokine-receptor domain of human ciliary neurotrophic factor receptor alpha, whereas d1o5dt2 is from the extracellular region of human tissue factor and is explicitly flagged “fr”: it lacks more than one-third of the common structure and/or sequence. Align d1o5dt2 only over supported homologous/structurally equivalent regions; treat unrepresented termini or elements as missing data rather than ordinary substitutions or family-wide deletions, and report coverage alongside identity or structural scores. For a canonical or template representative, prefer an unfragmented, well-resolved, nonredundant member such as d1uc6a1 over d1o5dt2 when other quality criteria are comparable; retain d1o5dt2 only when its particular tissue-factor subgroup, complex (annotated as complexed with cr9), or observed region is specifically relevant. Its partial structure can support local modeling but is unsafe as a template for absent regions or complete-domain architecture. The fragment flag does not revoke d1o5dt2’s curated family membership or the homology implied at that level, but truncation-driven gaps, missing strands/loops, reduced alignment coverage, and apparent compactness must not be counted as biological family diversity. Conversely, shared family membership supports evolutionary relatedness but does not justify transferring the distinct receptor/tissue-factor functions, interaction partners, or complete boundaries between these domains without independent sequence, structural, and functional evidence.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope__get_scop_service_info — /api/v1/; /api/v1/releases/current","mcp__scope__get_scop_domains — /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1uc6a1; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1uc6a1/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1uc6a1/annotations; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1uc6a1/homology; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1o5dt2; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1o5dt2/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1o5dt2/annotations; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1o5dt2/homology"]}]}
